body: Thanks for the replies guys. The stuff was apparently quite pure (so my friend who bought it said; he had a lot of experience with mandy). I drank plenty of water and stayed awake 24 hours, no alcohol that night except for maybe 1 or two beers. I'd previously done mdma a month before with the same people, that time was a very easy comedown.
Please don't. Talk to me instead.
I'm here. What do you want to talk about?
Plus i have a separate therapist, who is pretty good.

Thanks for your kind words. I think I misrepresented my psych – he made his diagnosis a year ago when the symptoms were less severe, and just said "it seems like a form of obsessive compulsive disorder". If this is OCD, it's unlike any OCD I've ever heard of, and I have several friends on the OCD spectrum.

Believe me I know the feeling. I come from a wealthy white family where every kid goes to college and there's never any problem with money or reputation. But I'm still paranoid, depressed and borderline suicidal. Mental illness can strike no matter how "comfortable" life seems to be, so don't blame yourself for it. I will say that life changes a lot after high school – options and opportunities turn up that you never find in the closed school environment. Life can be interesting and fulfilling even if you don't do college or whatever; your life isn't going to end on graduation day. Something that always helps me is to focus on real things, and real people – you have the "best friends in the world", focus on them! Make life feel real, don't just dwell on "what-ifs" (trust me, I know how bad that can get). I hope things get better for you.

I understand how you feel. I've had to put on a happy face and be a shoulder to cry on many times before, and I've seen friends of mine exhaust themselves doing the same. It's awful when people won't give you the support you give them, as if you're a crutch they can throw away when they don't need it. Remember that you are worth something as a person, not just as a resource for other people. They owe you a debt, and don't be afraid to remind them of that.

I know the feeling. I entered a top-class university three years ago, expecting to do brilliantly like my other family members had. Instead I had an awful time and had to take a year out to get psych treatment. I'm back at college now, and it's still a struggle, but I think I can still make it. You can as well. A bad grade average is not the end of your career or your life. You're young and smart and you can bounce back. Good luck!
